text:
Marathon Petroleum has climbed 11.3% over the past week and gained another 0.4% today, riding a sharp recovery from November 6th lows. The near-term tailwind comes from heating oil prices spiking 59% year-over-year heading into winter—a major demand driver for refineries that process crude into heating fuels. With refineries running at 95.2% capacity and diesel/heating oil storage sitting at 103.3 million barrels, tight inventories ahead of cold weather support margins for fuel producers like Marathon.

However, this strength sits against a headwind: Russian crude production has rebounded sharply, pushing global oil markets back into surplus as U.S. crude prices have eased to $89.62 per barrel. Higher crude supply tends to compress the gap between what refiners pay for oil and earn from selling refined products—the margin that determines profitability. The stock's recovery this week suggests the winter heating demand story is outweighing near-term supply pressures, at least for now.
